summary: This is a complete Hangman game implementation. It picks a random word from a list, then repeatedly prompts the player to guess letters, tracking which letters have been guessed and how many wrong guesses remain. The game ends when the player either guesses the word correctly or runs out of guesses.

explanations.15: array_rand() picks a random index from the array, so we can use that index to grab a random word from the list.
explanations.29: This uses the number of guesses left as an index into the $stages array to show the appropriate hangman drawing for that stage.
explanations.34: We loop through each character in the word by its position so we can check if that character has been guessed.
explanations.42: trim() removes the extra space we added after the last letter in our display string.
explanations.56: fgets(STDIN) reads a line of input directly from the keyboard that the player types.
explanations.58: We check that the input is exactly one character long and that it's actually a letter (not a number or symbol).
explanations.63: We convert the letter to lowercase so our comparison works even if the player types uppercase.
explanations.72: strpos() returns false if the guessed letter isn't found anywhere in the word, so we know it's a wrong guess.
explanations.76: We're comparing the revealed word (with spaces removed) to the original word to check if all letters have been guessed — this is a bit awkward because displayWord() outputs to the screen rather than returning a value, so we're capturing and processing that output.
explanations.82: We check if guesses ran out (hit zero) after the loop ends to display the loss message with the correct answer.
